test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 2 Feb 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In a given population, 20% of the population is affected with asthma out of which 90% of asthma patients used to work in flour mills. If 30% of the total population was working in flour mills, then what will be the percentage of the people working in flour mills who are suffering from asthma?
solution:
**Given:**

The population affected with asthma = 20%

Out of these 20%, patients who work in flour mills = 90%

The population working in flour mills = 30%

**Concept Used:**

Basic Percentage 

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the total population be 100

⇒ Number of people affected with asthma = 20% of 100 = (20)/(100)times 100 = 20

⇒ Number of asthma patients working in flour mills = 90% of 20 = (90)/(100)times 20 = 18

⇒ Number of people working in flour mills = 30% of 100 = (30)/(100)times 100 = 30

⇒ Percentage of people working in mills who are suffering from asthma = (18)/(30)times 100 = 60%

**Therefore, 60% of the people working in mills are suffering from asthma.**
